findings.title: Hung spawn flusher is never killed before being replaced
findings.body: Flusher workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, whose objects are SpawnProcess/BaseProcess instances, not instances of multiprocessing.Process. The isinstance check therefore never passes in production, so a worker detected as hung is not killed before _create_process_for_shards starts its replacement. The hung worker can keep polling and flushing the same Redis shards concurrently with the new worker, causing duplicate buffered-segment production and races between flush_segments/done_flush_segments, while the reference to the leaked worker is overwritten in self.processes.

findings.title: join() never terminates spawn flusher processes
findings.body: For the same reason as the restart path, isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is false for processes created through the spawn context (and for the threading.Thread workers used when produce_to_pipe is set, terminate is inapplicable). After join() waits until its deadline for workers that ignore the shared stopped flag, the terminate call is skipped, so shutdown can return while daemon flusher processes are still alive flushing segments and producing to Kafka; they are only cleaned up implicitly when the parent process exits.

findings.title: Invalid --flusher-processes values are silently remapped or crash obscurely
findings.body: The CLI option added for process-spans accepts any integer and SpanFlusher performs no positive-value validation. Passing 0 is silently changed by `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` into one process per shard, the opposite of an operator's explicit request, while a negative value makes num_processes negative, builds an empty process_to_shards_map, and then fails with a KeyError on `i % self.num_processes` during shard assignment instead of a clear configuration error at startup.
